title: Iridescent nightscape over La Silla
caption: Airglow and the Milky Way over the Swedish–ESO Submillimetre Telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: ESO's La Silla Observatory sits beneath a shimmering sky in this image. Deep reddish tones fill the right side and fade into the Milky Way, and a red and greenish-yellow glow colours the scene. In the foreground a silver dish takes centre stage: the Swedish–ESO Submillimetre Telescope, or SEST.

The colourful glow is airglow, light produced by Earth's own atmosphere. It is normally seen only from space or from very dark places, and La Silla has some of the darkest, clearest night skies on Earth.

SEST was retired in 2003 and no longer observes, but it remains a favourite subject for photographers, reflecting the lights and colours of the sky. Behind it is the rounded dome of the ESO 3.6-metre telescope, home to the planet-hunting instrument HARPS.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: Airglow is usually too faint for the eye to see well, but a long camera exposure gathers enough light to show its red and greenish-yellow colours clearly.

explore: HARPS, the High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher, is described as the world's leading exoplanet hunter, having found more low-mass exoplanets than any other planet-hunting instrument so far. The photo is by ESO Photo Ambassador Yuri Beletsky, an astronomer at ESO who takes such images in his spare time.
alt: A silver dish antenna in the foreground under a sky with reddish and greenish-yellow glow and the Milky Way, with a rounded telescope dome behind.
